record.original_question: Study the transformations that preserve random strings and random sequences.

evidence.quote: Study the transformations that preserve random strings and sequences.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\{0,1\}^*$ denote the set of finite binary strings and $\{0,1\}^\omega$ the set of infinite binary sequences, equipped with the uniform (fair-coin) measure $\mu$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra generated by cylinder sets. For a string $x \in \{0,1\}^*$, let $K(x)$ denote its prefix-free Kolmogorov complexity; call $x$ $c$-random if $K(x) \ge |x| - c$. Call an infinite sequence $X \in \{0,1\}^\omega$ Martin–Löf random if there exists a constant $c$ such that every prefix $X{\restriction}n$ satisfies $K(X{\restriction}n) \ge n - c$, equivalently if $X$ passes every Martin–Löf test.

A partial computable function $F : \subseteq \{0,1\}^* \to \{0,1\}^*$ is said to preserve randomness of strings if there is a constant $d$ such that whenever $x$ is in the domain of $F$ and $x$ is $c$-random, $F(x)$ is $(c+d)$-random. A partial computable functional $\Phi : \subseteq \{0,1\}^\omega \to \{0,1\}^\omega$ is said to preserve randomness of sequences if $\Phi(X)$ is Martin–Löf random whenever $X$ is Martin–Löf random and $\Phi(X)$ is defined.

Characterize, as fully as possible, the class of transformations that preserve randomness of finite strings, and the class of transformations that preserve Martin–Löf randomness of infinite sequences. In particular, give intrinsic (e.g. measure-theoretic, computability-theoretic, or combinatorial) necessary and sufficient conditions on $F$ and on $\Phi$ for the corresponding randomness-preservation property to hold.
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial partial results are known: almost-everywhere computable measure-preserving transformations on $2^\omega$ preserve Martin-Löf, Schnorr, and Kurtz randomness, and recent work (e.g. on continuous randomness via transformations of 2-random sequences and on randomness as an invariant under base/representation changes) extends the picture. However, a full intrinsic characterization of all randomness-preserving transformations of strings and sequences is not established, so the problem is partially solved rather than fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Algorithmically random sequence - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Martin-Löf, Schnorr and Kurtz randomness are preserved under almost everywhere computable measure-preserving transformations.
status_evidence.claim: Several major randomness notions are known to be preserved by a.e. computable measure-preserving maps.

status_evidence.title: Continuous randomness via transformations of 2-random sequences
status_evidence.snippet: Transformations of 2-random sequences yield sequences ML-random with respect to a continuous measure.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work studies which transformations send random sequences to random sequences in broader settings.

status_evidence.title: Randomness and invariance
status_evidence.snippet: Studies invariance properties of randomness under classes of transformations.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues into characterizing randomness-preserving transformations.
